claim: In January 2026 Coolify disclosed 11 critical vulnerabilities (CVSS up to 10.0) enabling auth bypass, RCE and root access, with ~52,000 instances exposed.
quote: Coolify, a popular self-hosted deployment platform, disclosed 11 critical vulnerabilities (CVSS up to 10.0) enabling authentication bypass, remote code execution, and root access, exposing over 52,000 instances worldwide to potential takeovers.

claim: CVE-2025-64419 (CVSS 9.7) allows arbitrary command execution with elevated privileges; CVE-2025-64420 (9.9) exposes a private SSH key to low-privileged users; CVE-2025-64424 (9.4) lets low-priv members run arbitrary commands; ~52,650 hosts exposed, disclosed Jan 5 2026.
quote: CVE-2025-64419 (CVSS 9.7) ... execute arbitrary system commands with elevated privileges ... CVE-2025-64420 (CVSS 9.9) ... low-privileged users to access a private SSH key ... 52,650 exposed hosts ... the trivial nature of the exploit make active exploitation highly likely

claim: An August 2025 bug deletes manually-added Docker volumes (permanent data loss) when a Dockerfile service is stopped/redeployed, because the 'Delete Unused Volumes' cleanup setting is enabled by default (coolify repo ~56.6k stars).
quote: Volumes get delete when stopping a service if `Delete Unused Volumes` is activated ... It looks like the issue is something similar to this older issue that was marked as completed #5343 but applies to Dockerfile services.

claim: A user broke Coolify by clicking the web-UI update button repeatedly (it isn't disabled after click), running the update script multiple times and losing their Laravel APP_KEY, rendering old projects unrecoverable with 'The MAC is invalid'.
quote: the button doesn't get disabled. It seems like the update script starts running multiple times when you click it again ... the encryption key ... Error: The MAC is invalid ... This will be fixed in the next version.

claim: In beta.434 Coolify generated malformed Traefik routing labels (empty Host matcher, domain mis-placed in PathPrefix) causing 502 Bad Gateway and SSL failures, persisting across beta.418-434 and requiring manual config after every deploy.
quote: This bug makes Coolify unusable for production deployments without manual intervention after every deployment.

claim: Coolify's default Traefik v3.1 proxy fails against Docker Engine 29.x with a Docker API version mismatch, returning 503 for all hosted apps until fixed in beta.444 (Traefik v3.6).
quote: the default traefik:v3.1 proxy fails to communicate with Docker, resulting in 503 errors ... client version 1.24 is too old. Minimum supported API version is 1.44

claim: HN commenters reported Coolify had so many Docker-deployment bugs they couldn't trust it in production, plus a long-standing unfixed issue of random CPU spikes to 100%.
quote: I experienced so many bugs around docker deployments I just couldn't trust it for production ... There's also a long standing issue of random peaks to 100% CPU, that they don't seem to be able to fix.

claim: A 2025 production comparison found Coolify's flow required too many clicks, that stopping/starting an app triggered a full rebuild from scratch, and that the author preferred Dokploy for getting out of the way in production.
quote: Coolify's flow required too many clicks for me ... stopping and starting the app triggered a rebuild from scratch ... Coolify layers its own platform logic on top of Compose

claim: Coolify ran in production at thousands of companies while formally remaining in beta the entire time, with the maintainer admitting 'it has many' bugs that are fixed daily.
quote: thousands of companies have been running Coolify in production for one to two years already - formally, however, in beta the entire time ... This does not mean it has no bugs, it has many, but we fix them every day.
